overview: The Medford High School Building Committee reviewed feasibility study budget updates, approved outstanding invoices, and voted on design programming recommendations for the new school building. The committee approved space requirements for the dining and food service area, the Curtis Tufts therapeutic program, and the early childhood education program with several cost-saving space reductions.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: The committee approved the minutes of the August 25, 2026 meeting as amended to correct a typo and to capture a discussion regarding parking counts and debt decision points.

items.title: Budget Update and Approval of Invoices
items.summary: The committee reviewed the feasibility study budget and approved Leftfield and SMA invoices for August services totaling $115,000.

items.title: Dining and Food Service Programming
items.summary: The committee discussed the functional advantages and spatial trade-offs of a scramble servery versus a traditional line cafeteria before approving the food service programming recommendations.

items.title: Curtis Tufts Program Design
items.summary: The committee approved the Curtis Tufts therapeutic program design layout on the third floor of the new high school with a request to further investigate classroom sizes prior to October.

items.title: Medford Early Education Program (MEEP)
items.summary: A motion to eliminate the MEEP preschool space from the project was denied, and the committee subsequently approved several space reductions including eliminating the playroom and downsizing the laundry room.

items.title: Design Process and Schedule Update
items.summary: Matt Rice outlined the upcoming design process and schedule for integrating site design, exterior building massing, and entrance concepts with advisory teams through November.

items.title: Upcoming Meetings and Community Forum
items.summary: The committee announced that the next community forum would be a virtual, interactive Sustainability Charette on September 17, focusing on energy, materials, and water use.

subject: High School Programmatic Design Approvals
